title: Analysis: Russia Pivots Disinformation Operations to Coastal West Africa as Sahel Security Model Falters
detail: Africa Defense Forum reported on August 25, 2026 that Russia is redirecting the influence-operation apparatus behind its Sahel foothold — exposed by the leaked 'Project Afrika' documents (published by Forbidden Stories and partners including France 24 in July 2026) — toward coastal West African democracies including Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Nigeria, and Senegal. The leak showed the Russian structure known internally as 'the Company' (run out of Saint Petersburg by Africa Politology, originally built by the Wagner Group before Russia's security services absorbed it in 2023) planted 644 articles containing propaganda or false information in at least 35 media outlets across Central and West Africa between June and November 2024, at a cost exceeding $300,000. In Senegal, PressAfrik head of publication Ibrahima Lissa Faye said his outlet unknowingly ran 13 Russian-funded articles, which he said 'appear to have slipped through our editorial validation process' and were 'intended to manipulate opinion.' Joseph Siegle, director of research at the Africa Center for Strategic Studies, said Russia is using the same propaganda playbook that undermined democratic institutions and promoted military rule in Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger as a foothold strategy for coastal states, following the demonstrated failure of Africa Corps mercenaries to secure Sahelian juntas against JNIM's 2026 offensives.
